issues.legal_issue: A prescribed authority cannot alter a landowner’s timely selection of permissible area when the authority’s power to make a selection arises only upon the landowner’s failure to select.
material_facts: The landowner did not make a reservation within the period allowed for reservation under the Act.
The landowner submitted Form E selecting his permissible area within the applicable period.
In determining surplus area, the authority included land that had been transferred to purchasers in the landowner’s selected area, despite his objection.
issues.conclusion: The Form E intimation was a selection of permissible area, not a reservation. Because the landowner had made that selection, the authority had no power to alter it; its order was without jurisdiction and a nullity.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(1) and 5(3) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, reservation was distinct from selection and had to be intimated within six months of the Act’s commencement; the prescribed form for reservation was Annexure B under the 1953 Rules. Sections 5-A and 5-B, read with rule 4 and Form E of the 1956 Rules, allowed a landowner who had not exercised the reservation right to select permissible area. Section 5-B(2) empowered the prescribed authority to select only if the landowner had failed to select under section 5-B(1). The definition of surplus area in section 2(5-a) governs the calculation where no area has been lawfully reserved. Gurcharan Singh v. Prithi Singh was distinguished because the landowner there had made neither a reservation nor a selection within the prescribed period, so the authority’s selection power was engaged.

predicates.surplus_area_determination: The proceeding determines the surplus area of a landowner.
predicates.landowner_made_timely_permissible_area_s: The landowner selected and communicated the area he would retain within the applicable period.
predicates.authority_changed_that_selection: The authority altered the landowner’s communicated selection when determining the surplus area.

issues.definition: When a surplus-area determination involves a timely selection by the landowner and the authority changes that selection, the authority’s order is without jurisdiction and void.

issues.legal_issue: Purchasers who acquired transferred land with knowledge of the landowner’s holdings and the legal risks cannot require the landowner’s permissible-area selection to be altered to accommodate their interests in the absence of a contrary representation or conduct.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired the transferred land with knowledge of the extent of the landowner’s holdings and the consequences that could follow under the Act.
Neither the landowner nor the transferor represented that the transferred land would be included in the landowner’s permissible area.
The landowner exercised the statutory right to select his permissible area, and the purchasers sought to have the selection adjusted in their favour.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers had no equity entitling them to require the landowner’s selection to be modified to suit their convenience.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5-B provides the landowner with the right to select permissible area where no reservation has been exercised, while section 5-B(2) permits authority selection only upon the landowner’s failure to select. Gurcharan Singh v. Prithi Singh concerns that failure-to-select situation and does not permit adjustment where the landowner has made a valid selection. A transferee who acquires land with knowledge of the landowner’s holdings and the associated legal risks, and without a representation that the land will be included in the permissible area, cannot rely on equity to modify the landowner’s statutory selection.

rule.if: transfer_purchasers_seek_adjustment and landowner_made_permissible_area_selection and purchasers_knew_landholding_and_legal_risks and no_assurance_of_inclusion_was_made

predicates.transfer_purchasers_seek_adjustment: Purchasers of transferred land seek an adjustment of the landowner’s permissible-area selection in their favour.
predicates.landowner_made_permissible_area_selectio: The landowner exercised the right to select the area he would retain.
predicates.purchasers_knew_landholding_and_legal_ri: The purchasers knew the extent of the landowner’s holdings and the legal risks affecting the transferred land.
predicates.no_assurance_of_inclusion_was_made: Neither the landowner nor the transferor represented that the transferred land would be included in the landowner’s permissible area.

issues.definition: Purchasers seeking an adjustment cannot require the landowner’s selection to be modified when the landowner selected an area, the purchasers knew the relevant holdings and risks, and no assurance of inclusion was made.

issues.legal_issue: Including transferred land in a landowner’s surplus area does not, by itself, extinguish the transferee’s ownership of that land.
material_facts: The land transferred to the purchasers was included in the landowner’s surplus area.
The purchasers held ownership of the transferred land.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion of the land in the surplus area did not affect the purchasers’ right of ownership, although it enabled the authorities to settle tenants on the land as permitted by law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished the consequences of classifying transferred land as surplus from the transferee’s ownership: surplus classification enables the authorities to settle tenants as permitted by the Act but does not itself affect the transferee’s ownership.

predicates.transferee_owns_transferred_land: A transferee holds ownership of land acquired from another person.
predicates.transferred_land_is_included_in_surplus_: The transferred land is included in the transferor’s surplus area.

issues.definition: When a transferee owns land that is included in the transferor’s surplus area, that inclusion does not itself affect the transferee’s ownership.
